readmeExcerpt:
# LiteBox

> A security-focused library OS

> [!NOTE]  
> This project is currently actively evolving and improving. While we are
> working toward a stable release, some APIs and interfaces may change as the
> design continues to mature. You are welcome to explore and experiment, but if
> you need long-term stability, it may be best to wait for a stable release, or
> be prepared to adapt to updates along the way.

LiteBox is a sandboxing library OS that drastically cuts down the interface to the host, thereby reducing attack surface.  It focuses on easy interop of various "North" shims and "South" platforms.  LiteBox is designed for usage in both kernel and non-kernel scenarios.

LiteBox exposes a Rust-y [`nix`](https://docs.rs/nix)/[`rustix`](https://docs.rs/rustix)-inspired "North" interface when it is provided a `Platform` interface at its "South".  These interfaces allow for a wide variety of use-cases, easily allowing for connection between any of the North--South pairs.

Example use cases include:
- Running unmodified Linux programs on Windows
- Sandboxing Linux applications on Linux
- Run programs on top of SEV SNP
- Running OP-TEE programs on Linux
- Running on LVBS

aiSummary.oneLiner: A lightweight, secure sandbox environment for executing untrusted code safely.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Litebox provides a minimal, secure environment for running arbitrary, potentially malicious code. It uses lightweight virtualization and kernel-level isolation techniques to ensure that the executed code cannot access the host system or network. The tool is designed to be extremely fast to start and stop, making it suitable for high-throughput automated testing or security analysis. It offers a simple API to configure the sandbox constraints and retrieve execution results.
keyFeatures: Kernel-level Isolation: Uses advanced OS features to completely isolate the execution environment.
Fast Startup: Boots in milliseconds, ideal for ephemeral execution.
Configurable Constraints: Allows fine-grained control over CPU, memory, and filesystem access.
Network Isolation: Prevents untrusted code from communicating with the outside world.
Simple API: Easy to integrate into automated pipelines or security tools.

useCases.title: Secure Microservices
useCases.description: Wrap individual components in a secure sandbox to limit blast radius.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Security researchers, platform engineers, and developers who need to run untrusted code safely. Requires familiarity with system administration and virtualization concepts.
